correctness.rationale: For any nonzero k, eliminating the affine flux variable produces cos(pi(nu x - Phi/k2))=g(x), where g=O(1/x), g'=O(1/x^2) for any target. The cosine changes sign at every high-cell boundary; its derivative dominates g' in the central root region and proves exactly one root per high cell. Analytic isolation excludes infinitely many low-cell roots or accumulation near zero (the A=0 case is handled by dividing out x), yielding count nu R+O(1). The Jacobian equals -k2 times the derivative of the reduced equation, nonzero for all high roots. Taylor expansion proves the inverse lattice correction. At k=0 the first-coordinate function has a single maximum at x=2 and at most two inverses. The actual standalone symbolic/numerical checker passed; no finite experiment is used to prove an infinite claim.

value.rationale: The natural question is whether a small cosine-memory perturbation retains the finite-to-one inverse structure of the uncoupled Chialvo map. It does not: any nonzero coupling makes the positive quadrant surject onto the entire plane, with infinitely many simple preimages for every target and an exact target- and amplitude-independent linear density of backward branches. This sharp discontinuity is a motivated global dynamical invariant, not a routine local Jacobian or sampled bifurcation observation. The explicit cell organization may matter for backward orbit trees, inverse-limit constructions, and the interpretation of bounded numerical neuron simulations.
